decisions.mark: names derive_scope in clew/scope.py as where the decision is resolved
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `derive_scope (scope.py:639)` ... "├─ derive_scope (scope.py:639)" | WHY: The answer names derive_scope in scope.py as the function that resolves the index scope (declared index_scope vs whole-repo fallback).

decisions.mark: states that a repository's own declared index_scope is preferred, and that every failure to find one falls through to indexing the whole repository
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "the index scope is decided by a `.clew.yaml` `index_scope:` section if one is declared and usable. If not, the scope is the whole repository" | WHY: The answer states the declared index_scope is preferred and that when it is not usable the scope falls back to the whole repository. It also covers the present-but-rejected case, which it handles with a warning and the whole-repo fallback (though it says a broken declaration is refused at the CLI level).

decisions.mark: conveys that the fallback carries a REASON explaining which scope was used and why, so an unstated scope is never silently guessed
decisions.detail: QUOTE: index_scope present but rejected → log WARNING, fall to whole-repo, reason says why | WHY: The answer's flow diagram says the fallback to whole-repo carries a reason explaining why, so scope isn't silently guessed. This matches the item, though only briefly.

decisions.mark: states that a Doxyfile's own INPUT is deliberately NOT used to decide the indexed tree, and explains why — a repository that ships one would get only its documented subset while a repository that ships none gets its whole tree
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Doxyfile | scope.py:683 docstring | Ignored for INPUT. Its ALIASES and PREDEFINED are still used | WHY: The answer says the Doxyfile is ignored for INPUT but never explains why (documented subset for repos with a Doxyfile versus the whole tree for repos without one).

decisions.mark: states that nested git trees are INDEXED and tagged rather than excluded from the scope
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Include nested git trees | `nested_repo_roots`, `_nested_trees_recursive` | Submodules and vendored clones are indexed, not cut out. Their own `.gitignore` is applied too | WHY: The answer says nested git trees are indexed, not cut out, but it never says they are tagged, and the item requires indexing plus tagging.

decisions.mark: conveys that the containment call was REMOVED rather than left in place with its callers dropped
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer never mentions a containment call being removed; it describes scope derivation only.

decisions.mark: states that the resolved scope is not the whole answer — within it, a file reaches the index only if something can read it, and names at least one of the two filters: the parse-built front end claiming the file types doxygen cannot read, or binary classification dropping files whose extension lies about them
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`_drop_binary_files` non-text files removed (cli.py:1745, filetypes.py)" and "The in-scope set is also passed on as `scanned_files`, which lets the JS/TS front end register files doxygen will not read (cli.py:1747)." | WHY: The answer says scope is not the whole story and names both filters: binary-file dropping and a front end that registers file types doxygen won't read. Its description of binary dropping doesn't mention extensions that lie about the file type, but the item only requires naming one of the two filters.
